props.title: Layering for Northwest rain
props.description: Three layers, two of which you'll take off. A guide by temperature.
props.author: Ballard
paragraphs: Rain here is rarely cold enough to be dangerous and rarely warm enough to ignore. The usual mistake is one big jacket. You'll be too hot walking and too cold standing.

Below 40°F: a wool or synthetic base, a fleece, and a shell. Between 40°F and 55°F: base and shell, fleece in the pack. Above 55°F: shell only, and vent it. The shell is the only layer that has to be waterproof. The other two just have to stay warm when they're damp, which is why we don't make cotton mid-layers.
If you're working hard, the shell is the layer you take off first, not last. You'll get wet either way; wet from rain is colder than wet from sweat because it keeps coming.
